text:
olivia: Starting onboarding for pelagic-6.5p (community checkpoint). Legal flagged a clause mentioning 'derivative binaries' and 'no commercial redistribution'. Can we serve a quantized 4-bit variant behind Dedicated without exposing binaries? :wave:

diego: Paste the license snippet please. The definition of 'derivative binary' is the key.

olivia: Here it is: ```
Redistribution: Model weights and derivative binary artifacts may not be redistributed for commercial use. Hosting the model for API inference is allowed provided binaries are not publicly distributed. Attribution: Any product use must credit the Original Authors and include a link to the LICENSE.
```

sam: From ML: we ran 4-bit GPTQ on a dev node. Latency ~2.3x, MMLU -1.6, Rouge-L -1.2 on our summarization set. Safety FPR +0.4%. Looks usable but need full eval sweep.

claire: Ops note: our artifact retention currently keeps build tarballs for 45 days and supports per-role downloads. We'll need to hide downloads and ensure backups don't create accessible copies. Also ensure Dedicated mounts do not hand binaries to the customer unless a license exception is in place.

legal: Quick read: the language treats quantized files as derivative binaries. Serving via API is allowed if binaries are not redistributed. For Dedicated where customers get disk-level access, we need an exception or a commercial license. Attribution requirement is straightforward. I'll write a short memo.

diego: Good. While legal drafts memo, ML can run the full eval and create a perf/quality matrix comparing fp16 vs 4-bit for canary decision. Also think about providing fp16 fallback route for safety-sensitive endpoints.

artifact-bot: Ingest scan: pelagic-6.5p artifacts found at s3://models/internal/pelagic-6.5p/2026-03-22/; detected fp16 tarball and no quant artifacts yet. Manifest tag: license=PEL-1. Public ACL: false.

olivia: Proposed immediate controls: 1) Block artifact downloads for license=PEL-1; 2) Add provenance header for attribution; 3) Enable embeddings endpoint (outputs allowed) separate from binary access; 4) Canary: internal -> Dedicated with contractual prohibition on binary export -> broader if legal OK. Thoughts?

sam: Sounds right. I'll run full eval suite (MMLU, HellaSwag, Summarization, Safety regression) and attach diffs. Also add prompt-level analysis to identify hallucination or safety hotspots.

claire: I'll open a pipeline PR to add a hard deny on export when metadata.license=="PEL-1" and a post-ingest scrub for any quant files that accidentally land in public buckets. Also add audit logging for any access attempts.

deploy-bot: Deployed branch "pelagic/quant-experiments" to staging-gpu-small. Logs: https://ci.example/builds/9812 :rocket:

legal: Memo posted to compliance tracker: "Serving is allowed for PEL-1 as long as derivative binaries (including quantized weights) are not redistributed. For Dedicated customer-hosted scenarios where customers receive files, require a signed exception forbidding downstream redistribution or deny binary access."

diego: Nice. Two operational follow-ups: a) Claire add upload-policy hook to reject exports and flag license in model registry; b) Olivia update onboarding checklist to require attribution text and provenance header format.

olivia: Draft attribution: "Pelagic-6.5P 1; Pelagic Research Collective. Licensed under PEL-1. See LICENSE." Proposed provenance header: `X-Model-Source: pelagic-6.5p;license=PEL-1;quantized=4bit;artifact=2026-03-22`.

sam: Uploaded eval diffs: https://artifacts.internal/pelagic-6.5p/evals/2026-03-22-quant-diffs.csv 1; MMLU: 61.2 -> 59.6, HellaSwag 84.0 -> 83.0, Rouge-L -1.2, Safety FPR +0.4. I'll add per-prompt failure examples in the doc.

claire: PR for artifact export block: https://git.internal/p/infra/artifacts/+/519 1; implements deny_export when metadata.license=="PEL-1", schedules scrub jobs for public buckets, and restricts download links to roles [security, compliance].

artifact-bot: Scheduled scrub job id=1314 for s3://models/internal/pelagic-6.5p/2026-03-22/quant/*. Will report on completion.

olivia: OK. Given legal memo and evals, next steps: internal canary only, enable Hosted + Dedicated serve-only routes, no download, include attribution in docs and provenance, add fp16 fallback route for sensitive workloads. I'll open the canary RFC once Claire's PR lands. Keeping thread open until RFC merged. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
